title: Courier Distance Charge Calculator
description: Build a courier charge from a base fee plus a per-mile rate with the Courier Distance Charge Calculator — quotes you can defend line by line. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a $6 base fee plus $1.85 per mile over a 12.4-mile job prices the delivery at $28.94 — a quote with its working showing.
quick_answer: The Courier Distance Charge Calculator builds a delivery price from the two parts courier pricing is made of: a base fee for showing up, plus a per-mile (or per-kilometre) rate for the distance. Enter your tariff and the job's distance and read the charge — quotable, explainable and consistent.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
A courier charge: base fee + (rate × distance), with the decomposition shown so the quote can be explained and repeated.
Is it free to use?
Yes — for quoting your own work or checking others' prices against your tariff.
How accurate is the result?
Exact for the tariff and distance entered. The commercial accuracy — whether your rate covers your costs — is set by your cost-per-mile figure.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Pricing follows distance; traffic is a time cost your tariff may handle through a waiting or peak item, not through this distance charge.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind. Quote on the road distance — it is the distance your wheels turn and your fuel burns.
Should the return journey be charged?
If the van returns empty, many tariffs charge a loaded-mile rate that silently covers it, or price the round trip. Decide which, state it, and apply it consistently.
Per mile or per kilometre?
Your market's unit. The formula is identical; the Delivery Fee by Distance Calculator frames the same pricing for food and parcel delivery.
Do I charge for the deadhead return?
Either openly (round-trip pricing) or silently (a one-way rate that covers it) — but decide, publish and be consistent. Customers forgive either; they do not forgive surprise.
What about multi-drop rounds?
Price the round's total road miles through the tariff once, or per drop with the base shared. Both are defensible; mixing them per customer is not.
Is a minimum charge normal?
Yes — it is the base fee wearing another name, and it exists because short jobs still cost a pickup.
